claims.text: An ML interatomic potential combined with free-energy perturbation can accurately and efficiently predict solid- and liquid-phase free energies and fusion properties of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The proposed workflow can retain vibrational entropy in both solid and liquid free-energy calculations.
The proposed workflow can retain atomic anharmonicity in both solid and liquid free-energy calculations.
The proposed workflow can retain electron–vibration coupling in both solid and liquid free-energy calculations.
The ML potential will be trained on a limited set of ab initio molecular-dynamics data spanning 0.5Tm to 1.2Tm.
Free-energy perturbation will correct residual errors in the ML potential.
Fe–Ni is a binary subsystem for which TOR-TILD has been benchmarked.
Periodic recalibration at phase boundaries is part of the proposed workflow.
The trained ML potential can reproduce local atomic environments in both solid and liquid phases.
The trained ML potential can reproduce the vibrational density of states in both phases.
The trained ML potential can reproduce key features of atomic anharmonicity in both phases.
Rapid ML predictions of forces and energies bypass the need for full ab initio molecular dynamics over the sampled configurations.
Free-energy perturbation preserves the fidelity needed to capture vibrational entropy, anharmonic effects, and electron–vibration coupling.
The workflow will reduce computational cost by approximately 10–50 times relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
The workflow will achieve free-energy accuracy within approximately 5 meV/atom of ab initio benchmarks.
The workflow will predict melting temperatures within ±50 K of ab initio benchmarks.
The method is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy systems such as CoCrFeMnNi from 0.5Tm to 1.2Tm.
Validation against binary-subsystem results can establish the reliability of extrapolation to multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
